thread:
Acme SRE: Seeing a big uptick in 504/5xx from hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC, affects our payment pipeline, SDK retries are spinning. Example: 504s on batch generate.
Jade (support): Sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal request id or sample log line? Also which SDK & region?
Acme SRE: request_id=req_0a9f3d, sdk=python-0.8.4, region=us-west1. We see pattern: initial 200 then a flurry of 504s for concurrent requests (~80 concurrent).
Sam (sdk): Do you have client retry/backoff config? SDK default is 3 retries with no jitter if not configured. Could be amplifying the fanout.
Acme SRE: We use default. Our trace: backend returns an early 200 then stream closes and subsequent requests time out. Snippet: 
```
2024-04-02T09:11:07Z req=0a9f3d status=200 stream_end=connection_reset
2024-04-02T09:11:08Z req=0a9f3e status=504 upstream_timeout
```
Nikhil (eng-sre): Thanks — this smells like connection eviction on the edge when auth tokens rotate. Any token rotation events in your logs?
Acme SRE: We rotate every 10m. Rotation event at 09:10:59, matches spike.
Jade (support): Okay crossing two things: token rotation + client retries may cause a thundering herd on the gateway, and edge may be closing keepalives causing resets. We'll repro on our side.
DeployBot: Canary deploy v2.14 to us-west1 started 2024-04-02T09:09:50Z (info).
Eran (platform): Noted. I'll check edge proxy for keepalive half-close and auth-cache invalidations around that window.
Sam (sdk): Short-term mitigation for Acme: set SDK retry backoff to exponential with jitter and cap concurrency to 30, and enable token refresh pre-warm (refresh 30s before expiry).
Acme SRE: Will try concurrency cap and pre-warm. Any server side quick mitigations?
Nikhil (eng-sre): On our side we can apply a short-lived ingress circuit-breaker to limit burst handoffs to the runtime and enable graceful draining to avoid resets — applying now to us-west1 for that customer tag.
Jade (support): We'll keep you posted. Can you send a request example that reproduces the issue? A small script that launches ~60 concurrent requests is ideal.
Acme SRE: Pasted below minimal repro snippet (python):
```
import asyncio
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key="REDACTED")
async def r():
  await c.generate("hello world")
asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(asyncio.gather(*[r() for _ in range(60)]))
```
Jade (support): Thanks — team will run that against a sandbox and also capture tcpdump/edge logs.
Eran (platform): Early findings: edge showed a burst of 502/504 resets when auth-cache entries were evicted during token rotation, and downstream runtime returned BUSY for some connections. Suggests combined effect: rotation -> cache miss -> short auth lookup latency -> connection queueing -> resets.
Nikhil (eng-sre): Eng mitigation applied: ingress rate-smoother and temporary higher connection limit for tagged tenant. Please test again.
Acme SRE: Re-ran repro, initial pass looks better — 5xxs dropped from ~18% -> 2% but still some intermittent 504s.
Sam (sdk): Try the pre-warm token step — if SDK refresh happens before expiry it should prevent the auth miss window. Also set max_concurrency=30.
Acme SRE: Implemented pre-warm and concurrency cap, retested, 504s ~0.5% now. Thanks.
Jade (support): Great progress. We'll keep the ingress smoothing in place for 1 hour while we do deeper root cause. We'll open a follow-up with detailed timelines.
Nikhil (eng-sre): Action items: (1) add a guard to auth cache eviction to avoid simultaneous purges, (2) improve edge backpressure signaling to runtime, (3) add docs snippet for customers about token pre-warm and client concurrency caps.
Eran (platform): I'll file a platform ticket and link this thread.
Acme SRE: Appreciate the quick response and the temporary fix, will monitor and report back.
Jade (support): Closing loop soon — will post RCA and communication draft for affected customers. :thumbsup:
